name: Boeing 767
summary: Mid-size twin-aisle twinjet, now chiefly a freighter (FedEx, UPS, Amazon Air) and still a passenger aircraft with Delta and United; the KC-46 tanker is a separate military family.

wings: Many -300ERs carry tall blended winglets; others have plain tips
engines: Two large underwing turbofans (CF6 or PW4000)
fuselage: Short, stubby 7-abreast widebody — looks chubby for its length (except the longer -400ER)
Pointed, slightly drooping nose identical to the 757's
Two four-wheel main bogies; freighters have no windows and a large forward side cargo door
tail: Low-set tailplane; tailcone ends in a short point

tellTales: Short, fat widebody with only two engines
Pointed narrowbody-style nose on a twin-aisle body
Freighter versions with no cabin windows and a big forward side door

confusedWith.howToTell: A civil 767 has no refuelling boom under the tail or wing-mounted drogue pods and usually wears airline or cargo colours.
The 767 is shorter and stubbier with a pointed nose and tall blended winglets (if any); the A330 is longer with a blunt Airbus nose and small angular winglets.
The 767 is a short, wide twin-aisle body; the 757 is a long, thin single-aisle body on tall gear with the same nose.
The 767 is much smaller with four-wheel bogies and smaller engines; the 777 has six-wheel bogies, huge engines and a blade tailcone.

usCount.source: Airline fleet data (FedEx, UPS, Amazon Air/ATSG, Delta, United; planespotters.net)
